title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests Without Jank
gist: GitHub rebuilt the Copilot app's diff surface (separate deterministic code-row geometry from dynamic comment blocks) to open PRs with 2,200 files and 1M+ changed lines, as AI agents shift the bottleneck from writing code to reviewing it. The piece situates this alongside GitHub stacked PRs and third-party review tools (Graphite, Pullfrog, CodeRabbit).

insights.claim: AI coding agents are producing more pull requests than human reviewers can digest, shifting the software-delivery bottleneck from writing code to reading and reviewing it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Value in dev tooling is migrating from code generation to code review/comprehension; watch review-tool vendors and GitHub's review UX investments.
insights.quote: the bottleneck has moved from writing code to reading it
insights.locator: The post, by Principal Design Engineer

insights.claim: GitHub's stacked pull requests feature entered public preview on 30 July 2026, positioned explicitly as a response to oversized AI-generated pull requests.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Platform owners are productizing workflow changes to cope with agent-generated code volume, a signal of where developer-platform roadmaps are heading.
insights.locator: GitHub's own stacked pull requests went into public preview

insights.claim: Microsoft research cited by a DEV Community piece finds code review quality degrades sharply once a pull request exceeds roughly 200 lines, versus million-line PRs that AI agents can now produce.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Large AI-generated diffs likely escape meaningful human review, raising quality and security risk — supportive for automated review and PR-splitting tools.
insights.locator: a DEV Community piece cited Microsoft research

insights.claim: Third-party tools Graphite, Pullfrog and CodeRabbit are competing to own agent-era code review, and Codegen CEO Jay Hack argues the winners will be teams that redesign workflows around review, not code, being the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: AI code review is a crowded, emerging category; workflow redesign rather than raw generation may determine winners.
insights.quote: review, not code, is now the bottleneck
insights.locator: Third-party tools have filled the gap

insights.claim: GitHub rebuilt the diff surface in the GitHub Copilot app so it can open a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and more than 400 inline review comments without janky waiting.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: GitHub is investing in front-end performance specifically to make huge AI-generated PRs reviewable inside Copilot, reinforcing Copilot as the review hub.
insights.locator: GitHub engineering has published a detailed account

insights.claim: GitHub's Copilot app diff renderer splits a pull request into two domains: fixed-height code rows whose geometry is computed up front, and variable-height comment blocks keyed by identity (file, line, side) and measured in an idle-gated batch pass scoped to roughly 2,400 pixels around the viewport.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A reusable pattern for rendering huge mixed-content documents in web apps; relevant to any vendor building large-scale review or document UIs.
insights.locator: At the heart of the rebuild

insights.claim: GitHub's first attempt using one ResizeObserver per comment block created a feedback loop whose cost grew with every mounted block; the shipped design makes observers flag rather than write heights, except frame-synchronously for user toggles.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Naive per-element resize observation does not scale; useful engineering lesson for front-end performance at scale.
insights.locator: Gimeno is open about an early mistake

insights.claim: GitHub's files-changed team reported in April 2026 that unified-view diff lines previously rendered as roughly eight React components and ten DOM elements each, and cut both roughly in half.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Shows component/DOM overhead per row is a key lever for React performance at scale.
insights.locator: The work builds on an April 2026 post

insights.claim: GitHub enforces the Copilot app diff surface's performance invariants with permanent structured probes run as CI budgets against a synthetic huge-PR fixture, plus an autopilot that drives the real desktop app so an agent can read on-disk logs and spot regressions unattended.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Agents are being used to close the performance-regression loop without humans, a pattern other engineering orgs may copy.
insights.locator: The team also describes the measurement loop
